findings.title: retryCount update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new catch block performs `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without any protection. If the original error was a database connectivity problem, this update will fail too; and if the reminder row was deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update (e.g. the booking was cancelled and its workflow reminders removed while the cron was mid-batch), `update` throws P2025 because the record no longer exists. Because this throw happens inside the catch handler, it propagates out of the loop and out of `handler`: every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the endpoint returns 500 instead of continuing. Previously the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not take down the rest of the run. The same applies to the new `else` update at line 179 (inside the try): if it throws, the catch runs and its update throws again, escaping. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch (and/or use `updateMany`, which does not throw when the row is gone).

findings.title: retryCount incremented via read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both new updates set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run (lines 184 and 195). This is a read-modify-write: if two cron executions overlap (a long run processing many Twilio calls overlapping the next scheduled run), both can read the same value and one increment is lost, so a failing reminder is retried more than the intended two times before deletion, and the delete threshold (`retryCount > 1`) is reached later than designed. Prisma supports an atomic operator for this: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which also removes the need to select `retryCount` in the initial query.

findings.title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: In the `deleteMany`, the new second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, unlike the sibling branch which is restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This cron job only manages SMS reminders (its query, its Twilio scheduling, and the only code that increments `retryCount` are all SMS-specific), but as written it will delete any `WorkflowReminder` row of any method — EMAIL or WHATSAPP, with any scheduledDate — as soon as its `retryCount` exceeds 1. Today `retryCount` is only ever written by this handler so nothing else can reach that state, but the column is generic on the model and the query's target set is broader than what this job owns; any future writer of `retryCount` (e.g. retries for email reminders) would have those rows silently deleted by the SMS cron. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retry branch.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/delete behavior
findings.body: The PR changes cron behavior in three ways — incrementing `retryCount` on failure (both on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result and on a thrown error), and deleting reminders once `retryCount > 1` — but adds no tests. The deletion threshold (`gt: 1` = exactly two attempts) and the fact that a reminder that fails twice is never attempted a third time are exactly the kind of logic that regresses silently. At minimum, tests covering: first failure increments to 1 and reminder is kept, second failure increments to 2 and the next run deletes it, and a success after a failure still marks the reminder scheduled.
